sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带300件你最珍爱的传家宝去上班，你把一个DJ台变成了一个像活生生的、有50年历史的精美艺术品的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Conservatives have been deeply divided about how to respond to allegations of sexual assault against Judge Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 保守派对于如何回应针对法官布雷特·卡瓦诺的性侵指控一直存在深深的分歧。

sentences.en: Why that's starting to change.
sentences.zh: 为什么这种情况开始发生变化。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月25日，星期二。

sentences.en: Ross, before these allegations emerged against him, was there anything that essentially all conservatives agreed on when it comes to the nomination of Brett Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 罗斯，在针对他的这些指控出现之前，在布雷特·卡瓦诺的提名问题上，是否存在所有保守派基本上都赞同的观点？

sentences.en: They all agreed that he should be confirmed, I think, is the most reasonable way to put it.
sentences.zh: 我想，最合理的说法是他们都同意他应该得到确认。

sentences.en: Ross Douthat is an opinion columnist for The Times.
sentences.zh: 罗斯·多塔特是《时报》的一位专栏作家。

sentences.en: I mean, conservatives basically spent decades winning presidential elections, appointing Supreme Court justices, and then being really disappointed with how those justices ruled.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，保守派基本上花了几十年时间赢得总统选举、任命最高法院法官，然后对这些法官的裁决感到非常失望。

sentences.en: So conservatives basically spent a period starting in the 70s and 80s trying to build a kind of intellectual project that was associated famously with the Federalist Society to ensure that Republican administrations would sort of know what they were getting.
sentences.zh: 因此，保守派基本上从70年代和80年代开始花时间试图建立一种与联邦党人协会紧密相关的知识分子项目，以确保共和党政府某种程度上知道他们会得到什么。

sentences.en: And Kavanaugh, you know, he's a Federalist Society judge.
sentences.zh: 而卡瓦诺，你知道，他是一位联邦党人协会法官。

sentences.en: He's the guy who all of my conservative lawyer friends in Washington loved from the beginning and said, this is the guy we should nominate and so on.
sentences.zh: 他是华盛顿我所有的保守派律师朋友从一开始就喜爱的人，并说，这就是我们应该提名的人，等等。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So what has happened since these allegations emerged within the conservative movement when it comes to Brett Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 那么在这些指控出现后，保守派内部针对布雷特·卡瓦诺发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I would say that there are, at this point, roughly three camps.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想说，在这一点上，大约有三个阵营。

sentences.en: What do you make of the, uh, all this Judge Kavanaugh stuff?
sentences.zh: 你对所有这些法官卡瓦诺的事情怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, it's hard to, it's hard to know what to make of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很难，很难知道该怎么看。

sentences.en: And the first camp, which, you know, shows up in figures as diverse as the Republican nominee for Senate in North Dakota.
sentences.zh: 第一个阵营，你知道的，体现在各种各样的人物身上，比如北达科他州参议院的共和党提名人。

sentences.en: These people were teenagers when this supposed alleged incident took place.
sentences.zh: 当这个假定的所谓事件发生时，这些人还是青少年。

sentences.en: Teenagers who evidently were drunk, according to her own statement.
sentences.zh: 根据她自己的陈述，这些青少年显然当时喝醉了。

sentences.en: They were drunk.
sentences.zh: 他们喝醉了。

sentences.en: Even if something like this happened, it was in high school.
sentences.zh: 即使发生了这样的事情，那也是在高中时。

sentences.en: It's not that big a deal.
sentences.zh: 这没那么大不了。

sentences.en: Maybe it was just horseplay.
sentences.zh: 也许这只是胡闹。

sentences.en: And, you know, there should be a statute of limitations for things that aren't actually rape and could be open to multiple interpretations and so forth.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对于那些实际上并非强奸且可能有多重解释的事情，应该有时效限制，诸如此类。

sentences.en: This is sort of, you know, boys being boys, high school records shouldn't matter kind of perspective.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是，你知道的，男孩就是男孩，高中记录不应该受到重视的那种观点。

sentences.en: And that's pretty common.
sentences.zh: 这很常见。

sentences.en: The difficulty that it's run into is that it's not actually the defense that Brett Kavanaugh himself is making, right?
sentences.zh: 它遇到的困难在于，这实际上并不是布雷特·卡瓦诺本人正在进行的辩护，对吧？

sentences.en: So this argument is sort of, on the one hand, pretty culturally widespread among conservatives and not only conservatives.
sentences.zh: 所以这个争论一方面在保守派中相当具有文化普遍性，而且不仅限于保守派。

sentences.en: I've talked to apolitical people who basically take this view, too.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过一些不问政治的人，他们基本上也持这种观点。

sentences.en: But it's a little bit irrelevant to the kind of defense that Kavanaugh himself has mounted.
sentences.zh: 但这与卡瓦诺本人所进行的辩护有点无关。

sentences.en: But I'm struck that while no senators are publicly saying, like, yeah, this is my camp, this is how I view things, maybe in part because, as you said,
sentences.zh: 但令我震惊的是，虽然没有参议员公开说，比如，是的，这就是我的阵营，这就是我看待事物的方式，也许部分是因为，正如你所说，

sentences.en: Kavanaugh himself isn't saying this, there are senators who are saying that their mind is already made up before the hearings are even heard.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺自己并没有这么说，但确实有参议员在听证会甚至还没听取之前就说他们的心意已决。

sentences.en: I'm just being honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我只是实话实说。

sentences.en: Unless there's something more, no, I'm not going to ruin Judge Kavanaugh's life over this.
sentences.zh: 除非还有更多内情，不，我不会因此毁了卡瓦诺法官的生活。

sentences.en: For example, Lindsey Graham.
sentences.zh: 例如，林赛·格雷厄姆。

sentences.en: And aren't those senators effectively saying this isn't disqualifying behavior, even if it's true?
sentences.zh: 难道这些参议员不等于是在说，即使这是真的，这也并非取消资格的行为吗？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: But I think some of those senators are taking the view that, you know, we already know from their perspective that this isn't going to be resolved, right?
sentences.zh: 但我认为其中一些参议员的观点是，你知道的，从他们的角度来看，我们已经知道这不会有结果，对吧？

sentences.en: That there isn't going to be some smoking gun or dispositive proof either way.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种情况，都不会有什么确凿的证据或决定性的证明。

sentences.en: What am I supposed to do?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么办？

sentences.en: Go ahead and ruin this guy's life based on an accusation.
sentences.zh: 根据一项指控就去毁掉这家伙的生活吗？

sentences.en: I don't know when it happened.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是什么时候发生的。

sentences.en: I don't know where it happened.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是在哪里发生的。

sentences.en: And everybody named in regard to being there said it didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 而且每一个被点名说在场的人都说没有发生过。

sentences.en: Again, that may be wrong, but that may be the assumption that they're making.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这可能是错的，但这可能是他们做出的假设。

sentences.en: And that in that case, they're basically taking a sort of innocent until proven guilty perspective, right?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们基本上采取了一种无罪推定的视角，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're saying, look, we're giving Kavanaugh the presumption of innocence and these allegations, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们说，听着，我们给予卡瓦诺无罪推定，而这些指控，你知道的，

sentences.en: haven't been corroborated by any of the witnesses the woman has put forward.
sentences.zh: 并没有得到这个女人提出的任何证人的证实。

sentences.en: So therefore, it's not enough to deny the nomination.
sentences.zh: 因此，这还不足以否决提名。

sentences.en: I think that would be the other line of argument they would use.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是他们会使用的另一种论点。

sentences.en: So from your perspective, a senator like Lindsey Graham isn't speaking in code by saying this isn't disqualifying.
sentences.zh: 所以在你看来，像林赛·格雷厄姆这样的参议员说这不是取消资格的行为，并不是在说暗语。

sentences.en: That's not code for I don't care about this.
sentences.zh: 那不是“我不在乎这个”的暗语。

sentences.en: He's saying in a legalistic sense, from what I've heard, I doubt the testimony will prove this beyond a reasonable doubt.
sentences.zh: 他是从法律意义上讲，从我所听到的来看，我怀疑证词能否排除合理怀疑来证明这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I don't want to speak definitively for Lindsey Graham, but I think that if you had him on this show,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，我不想斩钉截铁地代表林赛·格雷厄姆发言，但我认为如果你请他上这个节目，

sentences.en: he would say it's not that I don't take these kind of allegations seriously.
sentences.zh: 他会说并不是我没把这种指控当回事。

sentences.en: I just think they have to meet a test that, for instance, the Weinstein allegations met.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为它们必须达到一个标准，例如，韦恩斯坦的指控达到了标准。

sentences.en: These haven't met that teSt.
sentences.zh: 这些还没有达到那个标准。

sentences.en: Therefore, they're not enough to deny a person a high office when otherwise their reputation is sterling.
sentences.zh: 因此，当一个人的声誉原本无可挑剔时，这些还不足以剥夺他担任高级职务的资格。

sentences.en: OK, what's the second camp of conservatives?
sentences.zh: 好的，保守派的第二个阵营是什么？

sentences.en: How else did we see those on the right divide up when Dr. Blasey Ford came forward?
sentences.zh: 当布莱西·福特博士站出来时，我们还看到右翼有哪些分裂？

sentences.en: Well, the second camp is what you might call the sort of agnostic, uncertain and open-minded camp.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第二个阵营可以被称为某种不可知论的、不确定的和开放的阵营。

sentences.en: Judiciary chairman Chuck Grassley offered Ford a buffet of ways to tell her story.
sentences.zh: 司法委员会主席查克·格拉斯利为福特提供了多种讲述她故事的方式。

sentences.en: Either in an open session or a closed session or a public or a private interviews.
sentences.zh: 无论是在公开会议、闭门会议、公开采访还是私人采访中。

sentences.en: That's four different ways she can choose to come.
sentences.zh: 那是她可以选择前来的四种不同方式。

sentences.en: And this is the official view of most of the leading GOP senators, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是大多数主要共和党参议员的官方观点，对吧？

sentences.en: This is sort of Chuck Grassley's view officially.
sentences.zh: 这有点像查克·格拉斯利的官方观点。

sentences.en: It's certainly Susan Collins' stated view.
sentences.zh: 这当然也是苏珊·柯林斯陈述的观点。

sentences.en: Obviously, if Judge Kavanaugh has lied about what happened, that would be disqualifying.
sentences.zh: 很明显，如果卡瓦诺法官对发生的事情撒了谎，那将是取消资格的理由。

sentences.en: Jeff Flake's stated view and so on, which is these are serious allegations.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·弗利陈述的观点等等，也就是这些都是严重的指控。

sentences.en: We need to hear them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要听取它们。

sentences.en: If they are true, they're probably disqualifying.
sentences.zh: 如果它们是真的，那可能就是取消资格的理由。

sentences.en: Certainly, if now that, you know, Kavanaugh has denied them, if it can be showed that he's lying about that, then they're disqualifying.
sentences.zh: 当然，既然卡瓦诺已经否认了，如果能证明他在撒谎，那么它们就是取消资格的理由。

sentences.en: But they are just one person's word against Kavanaugh's.
sentences.zh: 但它们只是一面之词，各执一词。

sentences.en: So we need to hear them both.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要听取双方的意见。

sentences.en: We need to interview other witnesses, hear what they have to say, and then make a judgment.
sentences.zh: 我们需要采访其他证人，听听他们怎么说，然后做出判断。

sentences.en: So Camp 2 is basically arguing, if true, this is probably disqualifying, but we need to figure out if it's true, so let's find out.
sentences.zh: 所以第二阵营基本上是在争论，如果是真的，这可能是取消资格的理由，但我们需要弄清楚它是否属实，所以让我们找出来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's people who are, I think, open to multiple theories of what could have happened here.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些人对这里可能发生的事情持多种理论开放的态度。

sentences.en: They're open to the possibility that Kavanaugh definitely did it.
sentences.zh: 他们对卡瓦诺绝对做了这事的可能性持开放态度。

sentences.en: They're open to the possibility that this is some kind of mistake of memory, and they're open to the possibility that it's a fabrication.
sentences.zh: 他们对这可能是某种记忆错误的可能持开放态度，他们也对这可能是捏造的可能持开放态度。

sentences.en: But they think that all of those options are plausible given the limited evidence that we have so far.
sentences.zh: 但他们认为，鉴于我们目前掌握的有限证据，所有这些选择都是貌似有理的。

sentences.en: I talked to him on the phone today.
sentences.zh: 我今天在电话里跟他谈过。

sentences.en: And what did he say to you?
sentences.zh: 他对你说了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他没干那事。

sentences.en: And he wasn't at the party.
sentences.zh: 而且他不在那个派对上。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's clearly somebody's mixed up.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，显然有人搞糊涂了。

sentences.en: Ross, where does the idea of mistaken identity, that Christine Blasey Ford somehow is mistaking, misremembering that it was Brett Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 罗斯，认错人的想法——即克里斯蒂娜·布莱西·福特在某种程度上弄错了、记错了那是布雷特·卡瓦诺——这个想法是从哪里来的？
zh_words: 克里斯蒂娜·布莱西·福特

sentences.en: Do you believe the accusers at all?
sentences.zh: 你究竟相不相信这些指控者？

sentences.en: Well, I think she's mistaken.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为她记错了。

sentences.en: I think she's mistaken something.
sentences.zh: 我认为她在某事上记错了。

sentences.en: Where does that fit into this big camp number two that we're talking about?
sentences.zh: 这在我们正在谈论的庞大第二阵营中处于什么位置？

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I think it's the view considered by people who think that Brett Kavanaugh is likely telling the truth but don't see any clear reason why Ford would lie or fabricate the story completely and,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是那些认为布雷特·卡瓦诺可能在说实话，但又看不出福特为什么要完全撒谎或捏造这个故事的明确理由的人所考虑的观点，

sentences.en: in fact, you know, are aware that some version of this story came up in her marriage counseling sessions long before Kavanaugh was nominated and so on.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，他们意识到这个故事的某个版本早在卡瓦诺被提名之前很久就在她的婚姻咨询中出现了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so if you take those two views, if you hold open the possibility of Kavanaugh's innocence and you are charitable and assume that, you know, this isn't a smear,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你采纳这两种观点，如果你对卡瓦诺的清白保持开放态度，并且宽容地假设，你知道，这不是一场抹黑，

sentences.en: then a mistaken memory is pretty much the only explanation left.
sentences.zh: 那么记忆出错几乎是剩下的唯一解释了。

sentences.en: And it's also one that, you know, sort of fits, I think, with the cultural climate right now where there's, I think,
sentences.zh: 这也符合，我认为，目前的文化氛围，在这里，我认为，

sentences.en: a strong presumption against just saying that women who come forward with stories like this are liars.
sentences.zh: 有一种强烈的推定，即不能仅仅说带着这样故事出面指控的女性是说谎者。

sentences.en: And so you're not going to want to make that argument in certain cases, even if you think it's true.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些情况下，你不会想提出那种论点，即使你认为它是真的。

sentences.en: But I think the people, you know, the most famous case now.
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们，你知道的，现在最著名的案例。

sentences.en: Now, the story erupted last night after Waylon sent out a series of tweets, which he's since taken down.
sentences.zh: 现在，在威伦发布了一系列他后来又删除了的推文后，这个故事昨晚爆发了。

sentences.en: Ed Whelan, the sort of now very unhappy head of the Ethics and Public Policy Center, who tweeted that Professor Ford may have mistaken Brett Kavanaugh for a different classmate.
sentences.zh: 埃德·威伦，这位现在有点很不愉快的道德与公共政策中心负责人，他在推特上说福特教授可能把布雷特·卡瓦诺认成了另一个同班同学。

sentences.en: He looked at what Christine Ford told The Washington Post and figured out, OK, these people were named, these four people, where did they live?
sentences.zh: 他看了克里斯蒂娜·福特对《华盛顿邮报》所说的话，并弄清楚了，好的，这些人被点名了，这四个人，他们住在哪里？

sentences.en: And looked at what she had said and figured out what house it may have happened at because it was the house closest to the golf course.
sentences.zh: 并查看了她所说过的话，弄清楚了事情可能发生在哪个房子里，因为那是离高尔夫球场最近的房子。

sentences.en: A version of this mistaken identity theory that actually specifically identified another kid in Kavanaugh's class who looked like him and sort of fit what Waylon thought was the profile.
sentences.zh: 这种认错人理论的一个版本，实际上具体指出了卡瓦诺班上的另一个孩子，他长得像他，并且符合威伦认为是特征的描述。

sentences.en: Waylon actually named that classmate whom he suggests may have sexually assaulted Professor Ford, who was 15 at the time.
sentences.zh: 威伦实际上点名了那个同班同学，他暗示此人可能性侵了当时15岁的福特教授。

sentences.en: The man is now a middle school teacher.
sentences.zh: 这个人现在是一名初中老师。

sentences.en: I'm quite sure that Waylon himself thought that this was a totally reasonable explanation and expected that in airing this, you know,
sentences.zh: 我很确信威伦自己认为这是一个完全合理的解释，并期望通过公开这一点，你知道，

sentences.en: that he was going to sort of shake something loose, that he was going to get somebody who knew more about this to come forward.
sentences.zh: 他会打破僵局，能够让更多了解内情的人站出来。

sentences.en: Or that Ford herself was going to see this and say, well, maybe I did make a mistake, which obviously didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 或者福特本人会看到这一点并说，嗯，也许我确实犯了个错误，显然这并没有发生。

sentences.en: She quickly dismissed the idea.
sentences.zh: 她很快驳回了这个想法。

sentences.en: But I mean, from my own perspective, you know, the mistaken identity theory seems to me to be still, notwithstanding, you know, the foolish tweet storm,
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，从我自己的角度来看，你知道，认错人理论在我看来仍然是——尽管有那些愚蠢的推文风暴——

sentences.en: still the most reasonable way of reconciling the possibility that Kavanaugh is telling the truth with the possibility that she's entirely sincere.
sentences.zh: 仍然是将卡瓦诺在说实话的可能性与她完全真诚的可能性调和起来的最合理方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I have a hard time buying that the mistaken identity theory is something that people who have adopted it genuinely believe in.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我很难相信采纳认错人理论的人是真心相信这一点的。

sentences.en: It seems too convenient.
sentences.zh: 这显得太方便了。

sentences.en: It's the only one that allows it to be both ways.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一一个能让双方都说得通的理论。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But, I mean, that's true of a lot of theories, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，许多理论都是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's always hard to disentangle people's complicated motivations in coming to the theories that they hold.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在人们得出他们所坚持的理论时，总是很难理清他们复杂的动机。

sentences.en: But that doesn't necessarily tell you anything about the truth or falsehood of the theory.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定能告诉你关于该理论的真假或虚实。

sentences.en: I mean, look, the closer you get to the political process, of course, the more cynical actors get.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，你离政治进程越近，那些政客就越是愤世嫉俗。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you're dealing with the average senator, you know, they're probably looking at polls and just sort of, you know, thinking about, well,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你跟普通参议员打交道时，你知道，他们可能在看民调，然后只是，你知道，在思考，嗯，

sentences.en: what do my constituents want and how do I avoid facing a primary?
sentences.zh: 我的选民想要什么，我该如何避免面对初选？

sentences.en: There's so many imputations of bad faith and cynicism flying back and forth in this.
sentences.zh: 这里面飞舞着太多关于动机不纯和愤世嫉俗的指责。

sentences.en: I think it's worth assuming that even if people's ideas are crazy or dumb, most of the time they're not coming to them through a consciously cynical process on both sides.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得假设的是，即使人们的想法很疯狂或很愚蠢，大多数时候他们并不是通过双方都有意为之的愤世嫉俗的过程得出的。

sentences.en: I guess I'm just trying to parse.
sentences.zh: 我想我只是在试图剖析。

sentences.en: Do you see these camps as predominantly driven by principled thinking or by a strategic approach to how best deal with a situation and get it over with?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些阵营主要是由有原则的思考驱动的，还是由如何最好地处理这种情况并将其结束的战略方法驱动的？

sentences.en: I think that the main influence right now, it's less a sort of how do we get this over with and more a kind of tribal, we can't let these other guys win,
sentences.zh: 我认为目前的主要影响，与其说是“我们如何结束这件事”，不如说是一种部落式的“我们不能让这些家伙赢”，

sentences.en: which is slightly different.
sentences.zh: 这略有不同。

sentences.en: Because remember, look, conservatives are in a situation where if Kavanaugh's name is withdrawn, there can still be another nominee.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，听着，保守派处于这样一种境地：如果卡瓦诺的名字被撤回，仍然可以有另一个提名人。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, nominating someone else at this moment creates all kinds of political complications.
sentences.zh: 现在，很明显，在这个时刻提名其他人会产生各种各样的政治复杂性。

sentences.en: There's an election looming.
sentences.zh: 选举即将来临。

sentences.en: You might have to confirm them in the lame duck session.
sentences.zh: 你可能不得不让他们在跛脚鸭会议期间获得确认。

sentences.en: You know, you'd have to get Susan Collins on board with whoever you ended up nominating.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你得让苏珊·柯林斯支持你最终提名的任何人。

sentences.en: There are plenty of reasons not to want to do this.
sentences.zh: 有充足的理由不想这么做。

sentences.en: But if Kavanaugh is a wounded nominee, it's not like you're absolutely stuck with him.
sentences.zh: 但如果卡瓦诺是一个受损的提名人，这并不是说你绝对非他不可。

sentences.en: And what I see from conservatives is this sort of digging in based on what they perceive as the sort of unfair, unreasonable tactics of liberals.
sentences.zh: 而我从保守派身上看到的是这种基于他们认为自由派那种不公平、不合理战术的坚守阵地。

sentences.en: So it's not a sort of cynical.
sentences.zh: 所以这算不上什么愤世嫉俗。

sentences.en: How can we get this guy's through?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么把这家伙推上去？

sentences.en: It's the much more typical of our moment tribal.
sentences.zh: 这是我们这个时代更具代表性的部落主义。

sentences.en: You know, if these people are against Kavanaugh, we have to be for him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果这些人反对卡瓦诺，我们就必须支持他。

sentences.en: You know, if Kavanaugh has the right enemies, then I've got to be on his side or else those enemies will win.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果卡瓦诺有正确的敌人，那我就得站在他这一边，否则那些敌人就会获胜。

sentences.en: I think that's the main psychological dynamic here.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是这里主要的心理动态。

sentences.en: And what about the third camp, Ross, that conservatives are in?
sentences.zh: 罗斯，那保守派所在的第三阵营是怎么回事呢？

sentences.en: The third camp just says, look, this is a smear and we're sure it's a smear and we're not interested in sort of debating, you know,
sentences.zh: 第三阵营的观点很简单，他们认为这纯粹是一场抹黑，而且他们坚信这就是抹黑，没兴趣去讨论，你知道的，

sentences.en: whether he was a teenager and what difference that makes.
sentences.zh: 他当时是不是个青少年，这又有什么区别。

sentences.en: You know, we don't need to be agnostic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们没必要假装中立。

sentences.en: It's clearly a partisan hit job.
sentences.zh: 这明显是一次有党派背景的政治打击。

sentences.en: You can tell by the way the allegation was managed or mismanaged by Democrats in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 从参议院民主党人处理或错误处理这一指控的方式就能看出来。

sentences.en: And we should just confirm Kavanaugh because you can't be held hostage by these kind of smears or every nominee will be held hostage by them.
sentences.zh: 我们应该直接确认卡瓦诺的提名，因为你不能被这种抹黑绑架，否则每一位提名人都会被他们绑架。

sentences.en: And this camp, I should say, has actually gained momentum and support on the basis of the second allegation.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，随着第二起指控的出现，这个阵营实际上获得了更多的势头和支持。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: So Ronan Farrow and Jane Mayer published this piece in The New Yorker where a woman came forward saying that Kavanaugh had exposed himself to her during a drunken game that involved dildos or sex toys during freshman year at Yale.
sentences.zh: 罗南·法罗和简·迈耶在《纽约客》上发表了一篇文章，文中一名女子站出来称，在耶鲁大学大一期间的一场醉酒游戏中，卡瓦诺曾向她暴露身体，该游戏涉及假阳具或性玩具。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is that I think this camp has been strengthened and has grown because I think a lot of conservatives looked at that reporting and thought it was unconvincing,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我认为这个阵营因此得到了加强和壮大，因为我觉得许多保守派看了这篇报道后，认为它毫无说服力，

sentences.en: shoddy, and seemed more obviously sort of ginned up by a search for a second allegation.
sentences.zh: 粗制滥造，而且显然更像是为了搜寻第二起指控而故意炮制出来的。

sentences.en: And so they're reacting to that by essentially hardening their position by saying this looks more like a witch hunt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的反应基本上是立场更加坚定，认为这看起来更像是一场政治迫害。

sentences.en: And if that's what's happening, then we can't let it happen.
sentences.zh: 如果事情确实如此，那我们就绝不能任由其发生。

sentences.en: And it's a hit job.
sentences.zh: 这就是一次政治打击。

sentences.en: We have to fight it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须予以反击。

sentences.en: Can I understand, Ross, what makes conservatives, and perhaps you're among them, think that an on-the-record recollection of sexual misconduct,
sentences.zh: 罗斯，我想请教一下，是什么让保守派——也许你也是其中之一——认为这篇刊登在《纽约客》上的、有据可查的性不端行为回忆，

sentences.en: which was contained in The New Yorker, is flimsy?
sentences.zh: 是站不住脚的呢？

sentences.en: Is it the timing when it came out?
sentences.zh: 是因为它爆料的时机吗？

sentences.en: Because it is still a very rare thing in our culture to have someone say on the record, something happened to me.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们的文化中，有人愿意公开站出来说“我遭遇了某事”，仍然是一件非常罕见的事情。

sentences.en: It represents tremendous risk and fortitude.
sentences.zh: 这需要巨大的风险和勇气。

sentences.en: Certainly,
sentences.zh: 当然，

sentences.en: but I think this is a context where the authors of the story acknowledged that this was an allegation that was not brought forward but was sort of specifically pursued by Democratic politicians and staffers looking for another allegation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在目前的背景下，该报道的作者也承认，这并非有人主动提出的指控，而是民主党政客和工作人员刻意寻觅另一项指控的结果。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a whole discussion of how the accuser had deep uncertainty, more uncertainty than Dr. Ford about the allegation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，文中详细讨论了这位指控者对该指控的不确定性极高，甚至比福德博士还要不确定。

sentences.en: There is all kinds of evidence contained within the story about how people who would be, according to her,
sentences.zh: 报道中包含了各种证据，表明那些按她所说应该

sentences.en: in a position to confirm this story were unable to confirm it or denied it outright.
sentences.zh: 能够证实这个故事的人，要么无法证实，要么一口否认。

sentences.en: You have one confirmatory witness who claims to have heard about it secondhand, who won't identify himself.
sentences.zh: 你有一个声称从二手渠道听说此事的证实证人，但却不肯透露自己的身份。

sentences.en: And frankly,
sentences.zh: 坦白说，

sentences.en: you have the fact that our own newspaper had attempted to corroborate the same story and interviewed 25 to 35 people from this Yale class who might be in a position to be able to confirm the story and was,
sentences.zh: 还有这样一个事实：我们自己的报社也曾试图核实这个故事，并采访了耶鲁大学这个班级的25到35个人，这些人本来都有可能证实这个故事，但在

sentences.en: again, at the time The New Yorker ran with it, unable to confirm it.
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》发表该报道时，同样无法证实此事。

sentences.en: I mean, look, I forget about being a conservative.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，先别管什么保守派不保守派的。

sentences.en: I think there's a lot of journalistic uncertainty around the weight and credibility of the story right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在围绕这篇报道的分量和可信度，存在很多新闻界的不确定性。

sentences.en: That may change tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 这种情况明天可能会变。

sentences.en: It may change between when we're having this conversation and when it goes live online.
sentences.zh: 在我们谈话和这篇报道在网上发布之间，它可能就会发生变化。

sentences.en: But I think that the neutral reader should be able to see in that story certainly reasons to believe that it might be accurate,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，一个中立的读者在看那篇报道时，肯定能看出它可能属实的理由，

sentences.en: but also reasons to see why it looks like a fishing expedition with a lot of uncertainty around it.
sentences.zh: 但也能看出为什么它看起来像是一场捕风捉影的调查，周围充满了不确定性。

sentences.en: And again, I think that if you're sort of in Kavanaugh's camp in any sense, that's going to make you more skeptical of it.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我认为如果你站在卡瓦诺这一边，这只会让你对它更加怀疑。

sentences.en: But the first allegation remains as credible now as it ever was.
sentences.zh: 但第一起指控依然如最初一样具有可信度。

sentences.en: So from the conservative point of view, why would a second allegation on top of a deeply troubling first allegation undermine rather than strengthen the case against Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 那么从保守派的角度来看，为什么在极其困扰的第一起指控之上再出现第二起指控，反而会削弱而不是加强反对卡瓦诺的立场呢？

sentences.en: Why wouldn't we think there's no reason to doubt her?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不认为没有理由怀疑她呢？

sentences.en: So why would we doubt this second woman?
sentences.zh: 那我们又为什么要怀疑这第二个女人呢？

sentences.en: First of all, I think there are some reasons to doubt the first allegation, namely that, you know,
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为有几个理由可以怀疑第一起指控，也就是，你知道的，

sentences.en: we've been unable to find any sort of confirmatory evidence from the people that Dr. Ford herself named, including one of her friends, as potentially able to confirm it.
sentences.zh: 我们无法从福德博士自己点名的人（包括她的一位朋友）那里找到任何形式的佐证，而这些人本被认为能够证实此事。

sentences.en: So there's already some doubt about that allegation.
sentences.zh: 所以这项指控本身就已经存在一些疑问了。

sentences.en: And so then you get a second allegation and it seems less credible and more created by a partisan atmosphere than the first one.
sentences.zh: 紧接着又出现了第二起指控，相比第一起，它显得更不可信，更像是党派氛围催生出来的产物。

sentences.en: I don't think it's at all surprising that that would make people who have reasons to believe Kavanaugh or be committed to him feel that this feels more like a witch hunt,
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全不令人意外，对于那些有理由相信卡瓦诺或坚定支持他的人来说，这会让他们觉得这更像是一场政治迫害，

sentences.en: basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: It's not entirely fair, but I think it's sort of psychologically inevitable that that makes you cast more doubt on the first one as well.
sentences.zh: 这虽然不太公平，但我认为从心理学角度来看这是不可避免的，这会让你对第一起指控也产生更多的怀疑。

sentences.en: So the bottom line here, where it stands right now, is that you believe that for conservatives who were skeptical,
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，就目前的形势而言，你认为对于原本持怀疑态度的保守派来说，

sentences.en: this gives them a reason to lean into that skepticism and Camp 3 grows and Camp 2 shrinks.
sentences.zh: 这给他们提供了一个倾向于这种怀疑的理由，第三阵营在壮大，第二阵营在缩小。

sentences.en: As of right now, pending developments tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 就目前而言，还要看明天的发展。

sentences.en: Yes, I would say there's a stronger rally around the nominee than there was before.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为围绕这位提名人的声势比以前更强了。

sentences.en: Do you think that Me Too, as a cultural movement, has caused any of these conservatives to make a different choice than they would have before Me Too?
sentences.zh: 你认为“我也是”（Me Too）作为一场文化运动，是否导致其中一些保守派做出了与“Me Too”之前不同的选择？

sentences.en: And if so,
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，

sentences.en: do you think it's because they had an authentic reaction to Me Too or just simply because they understand that politically the way you treat a woman's allegation has changed?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是因为他们对“Me Too”有了真实的反应，还是仅仅因为他们明白在政治上对待女性指控的方式已经变了？

sentences.en: I don't think that you can meaningfully separate those two impulses.
sentences.zh: 我认为你无法将这两种冲动完全剥离开来。

sentences.en: I think that undoubtedly lots of conservatives were perhaps more willing to credit allegations against Kavanaugh than they would have been similar allegations 25 or 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，许多保守派可能比25到30年前更愿意相信针对卡瓦诺的指控。

sentences.en: And that is connected to what's happened in our culture and what Me Too has exposed.
sentences.zh: 这与我们的文化中发生的事情以及“Me Too”所揭露的现象息息相关。

sentences.en: But I don't think parsing the sort of sincerity versus the pragmatism or cynicism really reflects how the human mind works.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，再去分析究竟是真诚还是实用主义或犬儒主义，并不能真正反映人类大脑的运作方式。

sentences.en: The human mind sort of internalizes things.
sentences.zh: 人类的大脑会将事物内化。

sentences.en: And in your conscious mind, you are responding in a principled and above board way.
sentences.zh: 在你的意识层面，你的反应是讲原则且正派的。

sentences.en: And maybe in your subconscious mind, you're sort of manipulating things so that the politics all fit together.
sentences.zh: 也许在你的潜意识里，你在对事物进行某种操控，好让政治利益能够契合在一起。

sentences.en: But I think conservatives are just human beings like everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得保守派和其他人一样，也只是普通人。

sentences.en: And looking for the cynical explanation or the idealistic explanation is a mistake.
sentences.zh: 去寻找那种犬儒主义的解释或是理想主义的解释都是错误的。

sentences.en: It's all just muddled together.
sentences.zh: 这一切全都是混杂在一起的。

sentences.en: Ross, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 罗斯，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mike.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克。

sentences.en: It was a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸。

sentences.en: On Monday, conservative leaders rallied around Judge Kavanaugh, calling the latest allegations against him a choreographed campaign by the left to ruin his reputation.
sentences.zh: 周一，保守派领袖们纷纷声援卡瓦诺法官，称针对他的最新指控是左翼精心策划的一场旨在毁掉其名誉的运动。

sentences.en: But I want to be perfectly clear about what has taken place.
sentences.zh: 但我希望明确无误地指出究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: Senate Democrats and their allies are trying to destroy a man's personal and professional life on the basis of decades-old allegations that are unsubstantiated and uncorroborated.
sentences.zh: 参议院民主党人及其盟友正试图根据几十年前未经证实、也无佐证的指控，来彻底摧毁一个人的个人生活和职业生涯。

sentences.en: In a speech from the Senate floor on Monday afternoon, Majority Leader Mitch McConnell challenged the allegation of a second woman, Deborah Ramirez,
sentences.zh: 在周一下午的参议院演讲中，多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔对《纽约客》首次曝光的第二名女性黛博拉·拉米雷斯的指控提出了性质上的质疑，

sentences.en: first reported by The New Yorker, calling it a, quote, last-minute smear.
sentences.zh: 称其为“最后一刻的抹黑”。

sentences.en: That, Mr. President, is where we are.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，这就是我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: This is what the so-called resistance has become.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的抵抗运动已经变成的模样。

sentences.en: A smear campaign, pure and simple, aided and abetted by members of the United States Senate.
sentences.zh: 一场彻头彻尾、毫无掩饰的抹黑运动，并在美国参议院议员的协助和教唆下进行。

sentences.en: A few hours later, Judge Kavanaugh and his wife, Ashley, forcefully denied the allegations of both Ramirez and Dr. Blasey during an interview with Fox News.
sentences.zh: 几个小时后，卡瓦诺法官和他的妻子阿什利在接受福克斯新闻采访时，对拉米雷斯以及布雷西博士两人的指控进行了强烈的否认。

sentences.en: What I know is the truth, and the truth is I've never sexually assaulted anyone in high school or otherwise.
sentences.zh: 我所知道的是真相，而真相就是我从未在高中或其他任何地方性侵过任何人。

sentences.en: I am not questioning and have not questioned that perhaps Dr. Ford at some point in her life was sexually assaulted by someone in some place.
sentences.zh: 我没有、也从未质疑过福德博士在人生中的某个时刻可能在某个地方遭到过某人的性侵。

sentences.en: But what I know is I've never sexually assaulted anyone.
sentences.zh: 但我所知道的是，我从未性侵过任何人。

sentences.en: In the interview, Kavanaugh was asked about claims that he and male classmates drank heavily and targeted women at parties.
sentences.zh: 在采访中，当被问及有关他和男同学在聚会上大量饮酒并以女性为目标的主张时，卡瓦诺作出了回应。

sentences.en: We're talking about an allegation of sexual assault.
sentences.zh: 我们现在谈论的是一项性侵指控。

sentences.en: I've never sexually assaulted anyone.
sentences.zh: 我从未性侵过任何人。

sentences.en: I did not have sexual intercourse or anything close to sexual intercourse in high school or for many years thereafter.
sentences.zh: 我在高中或之后的很多年里，都没有发生过性行为，也没有做过任何接近性行为的事。

sentences.en: And the girls from the schools I went to and I were friends.
sentences.zh: 我和我读的学校里的女生都是朋友。

sentences.en: So you're saying that through all these years that are in question, you were a virgin?
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，在所有这些备受质疑的年头里，你一直是个处男？

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Echoing conservative leaders, Kavanaugh said he would fight the allegations and that he has no plans to withdraw his nomination.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺呼应了保守派领袖的说法，表示他将对这些指控抗争到底，并无意撤回提名。

sentences.en: I'm not going to let false accusations drive us out of this process.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会让虚假指控把我们逼出这个程序。

sentences.en: And we're looking for a fair process where I can be heard and defend my integrity, my lifelong record, my lifelong record of promoting dignity and equality for women,
sentences.zh: 我们在寻求一个公正的程序，让我能够被倾听，并捍卫我的清白、我一生的记录、我一生致力于推动女性尊严和平权的记录，

sentences.en: starting with the women who knew me when I was 14 years old.
sentences.zh: 从那些自我14岁起就认识我的女性开始。

sentences.en: I'm not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我哪儿也不去。

sentences.en: Do you believe that President Trump is going to stand by you throughout?
sentences.zh: 你认为特朗普总统会一直坚定地支持你吗？

sentences.en: I know he's going to stand by me.
sentences.zh: 我知道他会支持我。

sentences.en: Called me this afternoon, so he's standing by me.
sentences.zh: 他今天下午刚给我打过电话，所以他是支持我的。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日商业简报DealBook的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市DealBook峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域一些极具影响力的人物，其中包括J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话发生时实时观看。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在NYTimes.com上直播部分精选访谈，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》App进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The Times reports that over the weekend, Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein told two White House officials that he was strongly considering resigning
sentences.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，上周末，副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦向两名白宫官员表示，他正在认真考虑辞职，

sentences.en: after it was reported that he had suggested secretly taping President Trump and discussed using the 25th Amendment to remove him from office.
sentences.zh: 此前有报道称他曾建议对特朗普总统进行秘密录音，并讨论过动用宪法第二十五修正案将其免职。

sentences.en: Rosenstein raised the idea of resigning with White House Chief of Staff John Kelly and White House Counsel Don McGahn.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦曾向白宫办公厅主任约翰·凯利和白宫法律顾问唐·麦加恩提出过辞职的想法。

sentences.en: By Monday, Rosenstein was so convinced that Trump was about to fire him that his staff drafted a statement about who would succeed him.
sentences.zh: 到了周一，罗森斯坦深信特朗普即将解雇他，以至于他的幕僚起草了一份关于谁将接替他的声明。

sentences.en: So far, he remains in his job, but is expected to meet with President Trump on Thursday to discuss his future.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他仍留任原职，但预计将于周四与特朗普总统会面讨论他的未来。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为我们准备节日期间的待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会一躺下就人事不省。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索收听《Wirecutter秀》。
